parts.text: Wait, I put `pub type Tokens = TokenStream2;` in a proc-macro crate. But proc-macro crates can only export macros; non-macro public items are not allowed? Actually a proc-macro crate's public API can only contain proc macros. Rust will error: "`proc-macro` crate types currently cannot export any items other than functions tagged with `#[proc_macro]`, `#[proc_macro_derive]`, or `#[proc_macro_attribute]`". So `pub type Tokens` will fail. Remove it. Also `use` is fine (private). Let me remove the type alias.

<content>
1: //! Procedural macros that build Rust source code as token streams.
2: //!
3: //! This crate demonstrates the standard codegen stack:
4: //!
5: //! * [`proc_macro2`] - a stable, testable wrapper around `proc_macro`.
6: //! * [`syn`] - parses the incoming tokens into an AST.
7: //! * [`quote`] - turns a Rust-like template back into a `TokenStream`.
8: //!
9: //! A proc-macro crate may only export macros, so everything generated here
10: //! targets standard Rust items (free functions, constants, inherent impls).
11: 
12: use proc_macro::TokenStream;
13: use proc_macro2::TokenStream as TokenStream2;
14: use quote::{format_ident, quote};
15: use syn::{parse_macro_input, DeriveInput, Ident, LitInt, LitStr};
16: 
17: /// Generates a function named by the supplied identifier.
18: ///
19: /// ```ignore
20: /// make_fn!(greet);
21: /// assert_eq!(greet(), "greet");
22: /// ```
23: #[proc_macro]
24: pub fn make_fn(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
25:     let name = parse_macro_input!(input as Ident);
26:     let generated: TokenStream2 = quote! {
27:         pub fn #name() -> &'static str {
28:             stringify!(#name)
29:         }
30:     };
31:     generated.into()
32: }
33: 
34: /// Generates `count` public constants (`CONST_0`, `CONST_1`, ...) whose values
35: /// match their index.
36: ///
37: /// This builds the token stream programmatically instead of using `quote!`
38: /// for the repetition, which is useful when the shape is dynamic.
39: #[proc_macro]
40: pub fn make_consts(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
41:     let count = parse_macro_input!(input as LitInt);
42:     let count: usize = count
43:         .base10_parse()
44:         .expect("`make_consts!` expects a non-negative integer literal");
45: 
46:     let consts = (0..count).map(|i| {
47:         let ident = format_ident!("CONST_{i}");
48:         let value = i as u64;
49:         quote! {
50:             pub const #ident: u64 = #value;
51:         }
52:     });
53: 
54:     quote! { #(#consts)* }.into()
55: }
56: 
57: /// Derives an inherent `describe` method returning a short type description.
58: ///
59: /// ```ignore
60: /// #[derive(Describe)]
61: /// struct Widget;
62: ///
63: /// assert_eq!(Widget.describe(), "a struct named Widget");
64: /// ```
65: #[proc_macro_derive(Describe)]
66: pub fn derive_describe(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
67:     let input = parse_macro_input!(input as DeriveInput);
68:     let name = &input.ident;
69: 
70:     let text = match &input.data {
71:         syn::Data::Struct(_) => format!("a struct named {name}"),
72:         syn::Data::Enum(_) => format!("an enum named {name}"),
73:         syn::Data::Union(_) => format!("a union named {name}"),
74:     };
75:     let text = LitStr::new(&text, name.span());
76: 
77:     let expanded = quote! {
78:         impl #name {
79:             pub fn describe(&self) -> &'static str {
80:                 #text
81:             }
82:         }
83:     };
84:     expanded.into()
85: }

(End of file - total 85 lines)
</content>
